beats.html:
Trick or treat
is younger than jazz.

The phrase does not appear
in North American print
until the 1920s.

One of the earliest
is a 1927 newspaper
in Blackie, Alberta.

Traditions get invented.
And recently.

The oldest looking part
of the night
is the newest thing about it.

beats.html:
Jack o lanterns
were turnips.

Ireland and Scotland
carved turnips and beets
for centuries.

Irish immigrants switched
in America because pumpkins
were bigger to hollow.
The ritual mattered.
The turnip did not.

beats.html:
Somebody decided children
deserved their own night.

Nickelodeon launched SNICK
in August 1992.

2 hours on a Saturday,
programmed entirely
for kids.

In the slot adults
had always owned.

It worked because it was theirs.
Not because it was gentle.

beats.html:
Casper built its lead
out of nothing at all.

1995. The first feature film
to carry a fully computer
generated character in a lead.

Every frame of him
was made rather than filmed.

A film about a ghost
nobody could touch.
They built him from air.

beats.html:
Victorians were frightened
enough of being buried alive
to patent a way out.

Safety coffins came with
bells, ropes
and breathing tubes.

Christian Eisenbrandt
patented one
in 1843.

A whole industry grew
around a fear nobody
would say out loud.

Fear does not stay quiet.
It builds things.

beats.html:
They put a stone
in the child's mouth.

A Roman era grave
excavated at Lugnano, Italy.

One of a set of burials
archaeologists read as meant
to stop the dead returning.

Every generation does
something physical about
a fear it cannot argue with.
Ours is just quieter.
